title: Slope-intercept form
status: draft: written by Claude, waiting for owner review

hints.lin.slope-intercept.read: In y = mx + b, m (the number with x) is the slope and b (the number on its own) is the y-intercept. Keep the signs.
hints.lin.slope-intercept.write: Find the slope and where the line crosses the y-axis. Then write y = (slope)x + (intercept).
hints.lin.slope-intercept.two-points: Find the slope first. Then put one point into y = mx + b and solve for b.
hints.lin.slope-intercept: y = mx + b: m is the slope, b is where the line crosses the y-axis. From two points: slope first, then b.

misconceptionMessages.lin.mb-swapped: m goes with x (the slope) and b is the number on its own (the y-intercept). Check you haven't swapped them.
misconceptionMessages.lin.mb-sign: Keep the sign: in y = −2x − 7, the slope is −2 and the y-intercept is −7.
misconceptionMessages.lin.intercept-x: b is where the line crosses the y-axis (the up-and-down one), where x = 0.
misconceptionMessages.lin.b-from-point: A point's y is only the y-intercept when its x is 0. Put the point into y = mx + b and solve for b.

sections.title: Read m and b
sections.objective: Read the slope and the y-intercept from y = mx + b.
explain: m is the number multiplying x; b is the number on its own.
The order they're written in doesn't matter: y = 4 − 3x has slope −3 and y-intercept 4.
sections.key: In y = mx + b, the number with x is the slope (m) and the number on its own is the y-intercept (b). Keep the signs.

sections.title: Write the equation
sections.objective: Write y = mx + b from a slope and y-intercept, or from a graph.
explain: From a graph: the y-intercept is where the line crosses the y-axis; the slope is rise over run.

visual.caption: Tap through: run, rise, slope, and where it crosses the y-axis.

sections.key: Find the slope (m) and where the line crosses the y-axis (b). Then write y = mx + b.

sections.title: From two points
sections.objective: Write y = mx + b for the line through two points.
explain: Find the slope from the two points.
Put either point into y = mx + b and solve for b.
sections.key: Slope first. Then put one point into y = mx + b and solve for b.

sections.title: Putting it together
sections.key: y = mx + b: m is the slope, b is where the line crosses the y-axis. From two points: slope first, then b.
